correctness.rationale: Enumerating all 2^r roots for r<=6 and all nine-square block concatenations is exhaustive. The square-block recurrence is exact by induction, and all outcomes use direct substring checks. The independent binary-prefix DP checks all potential words of length <=9*2*6=108 and obtains identical survivor sets for each root cap. Root<=5 gives zero nine-square factorizations; root<=6 gives exactly two, each root vector (3,2,2,2,6,2,2,2,3). The finite universal bound is proved from the hypothesis; no finite experiment is extrapolated to an unbounded range.

originality.rationale: Shallit 2026 proves maximal number nine and supplies a witness with root size six, and an earlier finite result establishes shortest total length 48 and two corresponding words. Neither statement implies that every nine-square overlap-free word has a root length at least six; smaller roots still permit much longer total length in principle. The current result establishes the sharp global local-root obstruction and the entire bounded-root equality class. Six mathematical research-record queries, relevant earlier mathematical claims, the published full text and targeted web searches found no covering theorem. Risks are explicitly listed.

value.rationale: Nine is the largest feasible number of overlap-free consecutive binary squares, so the minimum possible longest constituent root is a natural structural invariant distinct from minimum total word length. A 12-symbol square is forced somewhere regardless of total word length, and at that sharp root-width threshold the product is rigid (two complemented/reversed words, one factorization each). This classifies a natural boundary for how locally short the blocks of a globally extremal product can all be; it is not just a length slice or a table recomputation from the main paper.
